children: , the global automaker, fell about 1.7% to $187.05 in U.S. trading at 11am ET time on Thursday. Investors have a big factory question to weigh: according to Reuters, Toyota estimates that wider automation could cost roughly 1 trillion ($6.4 billion) a year starting in 2028.

That figure spans Toyota, its group companies and major suppliers. The company estimates they could need about 400,000 robots, including replacements for aging equipment and new machines for factory work and logistics. It is a striking scale, but it is still an estimate: Toyota has not committed to the annual spending or said how long it might continue.

At $187.05, the shares sit 10.07% below the $208.00 GF Value shown in the graphic. That gap catches the eye; the harder question is what a much more automated production network would earn back. Toyota has long described its manufacturing approach as people teaching robots to improve quality and productivity. Investors now need measurable gains in output, quality and costs before putting a return on this potential bill.

title: Toyota Drops 1.74% as Automation Bill Reaches 1 Trillion
